Grace Jones was in Spanish Town, St Catherine, Jamaica to [Marjorie Jones](link_52) (née Williams) and Reverend Robert W. Jones. When she was 12 she moved to Syracuse, New York, joining her family who had already moved there. She studied acting at Syracuse University and appeared in her first musical; halfway through college, she was approached by a drama professor who proposed that she work with him in a play he was putting on in Philadelphia, she accepted.  
  
Jones later moved to New York City and signed on as a model with Wilhelmina Models, but when her looks weren't successfully received, she moved to Paris, France, where her androgynous, bold, dark-skinned appearance was so highly visible, she began to model for [Yves Saint-Laurent](link_53), [Claude Montana](link_54), [Kenzo Takada](link_55), [Helmut Newton](link_56), [Guy Bourdin](link_57), [Hans Feurer](link_58), and [Azzedine Alaïa](link_59), and she appeared on the covers of "Elle", "Vogue", and "Der Stern."  
  
Disillusioned with modeling, and since she always wanted to be an actress, she began her movie career playing small parts, her first being in the blaxploitation flick [Gordon's War (1973)](link_60) followed by an uncomfortable cameo in the unwatchable French sex comedy [Let's Make a Dirty Movie (1976)](link_61). It wasn't until the the '80s that Jones' on-screen career really soared, when she appeared in three supporting roles: Zula, the amazonian warrior in the American sword and sorcery/adventure film [Conan the Destroyer (1984)](link_62); May Day, the secondary antagonist in the 14th James Bond film [A View to a Kill (1985)](link_63); and Katrina, a bloodthirsty Egyptian vampire queen in the comedy horror [Vamp (1986)](link_64). Leaving audiences with only the resonance of unique and tantalizing movie performances, Jones hasn't acted in a feature film since the '90s.  
  
In recent years, Jones's primary focus is sharing the vulnerability behind her larger-than-life persona. Jones and director [Sophie Fiennes](link_65) released the documentary [Grace Jones: Bloodlight and Bami (2017)](link_66). According to Fiennes, the documentary is not a retelling of what can easily be found in books and magazines, but an intimate portrait of Jones in recent years as she returns to Jamaica, the country of her birth and childhood, for a family reunion.

"The Harlem Sweetheart"

## EDNA MAE HARRIS

August 27, 2024

> After Micheaux showed the picture, we, the actors, would appear on stage and the people in the audience would be so glad to see us, the stars of Micheaux's film.

—Edna Mae Harris​

[![Image 2: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/edna-mae-harris-in-harlem-serenade.png?1724801001)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

Edna Mae Harris performs "Harlem Serenade" at a nightclub with Lucky Millinder's orchestra

  
​Born in Harlem to boxer and customs inspector Sam Harris and Mary Harris(née Walker), who worked as a maid, the youngest of five—who all entered showbusiness, with the exception of one—singer/actress Edna Mae Harris had a vast array of talents that stretched outside performing on stage, screen, or song, as it was in 1928 that Harris won the New York Daily News swimming championship.  
​  
Retiring in 1959 after marrying musician Bernard Flood, Edna Mae Harris had a career worthy of notice and knowing.  
  
Within the realm of entertainment through acting and music, Harris performed in almost every form and medium of entertainment. She could be heard and seen in short film "soundies" during WWII, but her film work dates back even further while in Harlem, performing in the Black vaudeville circuit, THEATER OWNERS BOOKING ASSOCIATION from 1929—1933.  
  
Living near the Lafayette Theater, notable entertainers Ethel Waters and Maude Russell (who lived to be 104!), who coached Harris "on her singing and dancing" (source: Harlem World), were at the Harris home frequently, encouraging Edna Mae to pursue a career in entertainment.  
​

[![Image 3: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-and-cameron-newsome_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

Written and directed by Oscar Micheaux, THE NOTORIOUS ELINOR LEE (1939). starring Edna Mae Harris and Carman Newsome

  
​A career that would soon take shape and elevate from Harlem to Hollywood in the form of appearing in major studio films—usually bit parts—beginning with**BULLETS OR BALLOTS** (1936) in an uncredited bit role as "Rose", **THE GREEN PASTURES** (1936), **THE GARDEN OF ALLAH** (1936), to co-starring opposite world heavyweight champion boxer Joe Louis in **SPIRIT OF YOUTH** (1938), a film mirroring his own life, and independent films by Oscar Micheaux;**LYING LIPS** (1939)—with frequent Micheaux actor Carman Newsome, along with other notable actors; Robert Earl Jones (father of James Earl Jones), Amanda Rudolph,Juano Hernández, and"Slim" Thompson—and **THE NOTORIOUS ELINOR LEE** (1940), again pairing Harris with Carman Newsome, Robert Earl Jones, and Juano Hernández, to all-Black casted films as **PARADISE IN HARLEM** (1939).  
  
Harris would speak highly of the Black pioneer filmmaker Micheaux, elaborating on her experience working in an Oscar Micheaux production, recalling the actors were paid anywhere between five or ten dollars a day, as it was a struggle both as a Black creative artist and as a Black creative artist funding his own films:  
  
_"_ _We got paid maybe $5, $10 a day. And we finished the movie in three or four days. We had to wear our own clothes.They did give us a sandwich for lunch, though. Oscar was a nice man. He and his wife. They were like ministers, watching over us. He had to do some of his filming in the South, too.Except he didn't have any studios there. So we'd go to people's houses and ask if we could use their living room or their kitchen."_  
  

[![Image 4: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/the-green-pastures-1936_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

On set during filming on THE GREEN PASTURES (1936), captioned from left as: Edna Mae Harris with co-star Joe Louis, James Fuller, director William Keighley, head electrician Larry Kennedy, co-director Marc Connelly

[Video 1](link_16)

Black History Month video edit by Dominique Breckenridge, including a clip of Edna Mae Harris(fifth to the last clip) in director Oscar Micheaux's LYING LIPS (1939)

Harris' acting stretched back to high school—Wadleigh High School—when she worked with a stock company doing dramatic sketches at the Alhambra Theatre before "her first break" in a Black-cast Broadway play by playwright Marc Connelly, **THE PASTURE** in 1930 (later appearing in the Warner Brothers 1936 adaptation).  
  
During her time in Hollywood, Harris performed and entertained just as much, if not more, offscreen, from performing at Harlem's Apollo Theatre, appearing there in 1943, multiple appearances in 1945, and 1954—which included being part of an onstage comedy act with comedian Pigmeat Markham—a vocalist to both composer and lyricist Nobl e Sissle and his Orchestra, saxophonist and jazz trumpeter Benny Carter, as well as with Lena Horne and Billy Banks.  
  
Her resume continues as in 1942 Harris appeared as "Mistress of Ceremonies" during a fourteen-week engagement at the old Elks’ Rendezvous, announced a weekly radio show over station WMCA in New York City,toured with other black performers—including Hattie McDaniel, who, at the time, was touring Black theatres promoting herself and her role in the film **GONE WITH THE WIND** (1939)—and made a contribution by providing "ch aracter dialect parts on many broadcasts for the Columbia Workshop Program."  
  
  

[![Image 5: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/joe-louis-and-edna-mae-harris_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

World heavyweight boxing champ, Joe Louis, greeting SPIRIT OF YOUTH co-star Edna Mae Harris[![Image 6: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/spirit-of-youth-film_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

[![Image 7: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/editor/edna-mae-harris-and-joe-louis.jpg?1724800217)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

Joe Louis and his SPIRIT OF YOUTH co-star Edna Mae Harris[![Image 8: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/spirit-of-youth_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

> I remember one big problem Oscar Micheaux had is that there was no place he could show his movies in New York. None of the big theaters, like Loews, would take them. We had to bring them to the colored theaters in the South. We'd all go, too. We'd show the movie, then the stars would come out on stage and talk about the movie. (laughs) They don't do that anymore.

—Edna Mae Harris  
Daily News, 1990

  
Harris would live 86 years, passing away in 1997 of a heart attack, but her name and contributions to the arts should be forever remembered.  
  

[![Image 9](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short_orig.png "Edna Mae Harris in T'AINT NO GOOD (1942)")

[![Image 10](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short-2.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short-2_orig.png)

[![Image 11](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short-3.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short-3_orig.png)

[![Image 12](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short-4.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/edna-mae-harris-musical-short-4_orig.png)

Edna Mae Harris with "Slim" Thomas in **T'AINT NO GOOD** (1942)

Sources:  
  
The Guardian,London, Greater London, England, dated Friday, October 17, 1997  
Harlem World,Harlem’s Edna Mae Harris, One Of The Legendary Entertainers During The 1930-1940’s, 1914 – 1997, dated April 25, 2022  
Daily News, New York, New York, dated Wednesday, January 31, 1990

[![Image 13: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/dominique-revue-logo_8.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

## Digital _Archives_

_The HistoryMakers Digital Archive_, developed by Carnegie Mellon University, provides unique access to thousands of African American lives…a virtual “Whose Who” of the African American community. More importantly, it takes you inside these lives to learn more about its history, organizations, communities and careers. Out of these stories is emerging a new and more accurate version of black history. See for yourself! Sign up as a DigitalMaker for $30 per month/$300 per year under _Get Involved:Memberships_ and gain access to what has cost _The HistoryMakers_ millions of dollars to create. You will be glad you did!

If STEM(science, technology, engineering or math) is your interest, then look no more! Our ScienceMakers Digital Archive, also developed by Carnegie Mellon University, offers unique **and free** access to the lives of over 200 of our nation’s top African American scientists and tech leaders! Gaining access is easy. Sign up as a BasicMaker under year under _Get Involved:Memberships_ and voila, our content is at your fingertips!

[The HistoryMakers Digital Archive](https://da.thehistorymakers.org/ "(opens in a new window)")

[The ScienceMakers Digital Archive](https://sm.thehistorymakers.org/ "(opens in a new window)")

## The HistoryMakers **on**_60 Minutes_

The achievements of historically significant Black Americans are at risk of going unpreserved, as important figures die without documenting their stories for future generations. 60 MINUTES’ **Bill Whitaker**explores how one organization is trying to prevent that by creating an expansive digital archive of first-person accounts of the Black experience. Marc Lieberman is the producer.

[READ MORE](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/historymakers-black-history-60-minutes-2023-02-19/ "(opens in a new window)")

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UfygzCvKj2U)

![Image 3: Julia Stasch Former President, The MacArthur Foundation](https://www.thehistorymakers.org/sites/default/files/2023-10/100-Most-Powerful-082-Julia-Stasch%281%29_0.jpg)

> I saw the update on your astounding story on 60 Minutes on Sunday. I was so pleased to see the robust relationship with the Library of Congress had come true. Just the right place for the precious assets you have been collecting. Congratulations to you for your vision and how far you have taken the dream.

Julia Stasch Former President, The MacArthur Foundation

## Creating a more inclusive **record of American History**

_The HistoryMakers_’ mission has been to **educate** the world about the history, lives, careers and accomplishments of African Americans across a variety of disciplines - the arts, business, civic engagement, education, entertainment, law, the media, medicine, STEM, the military, music, politics, religion, sports, and fashion & beauty - by making its content accessible worldwide and a free public website. With _The HistoryMakers Digital Archive_, users can access thousands of first person accounts of African American leaders from desktop, portable devices, and smart phones 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, anywhere in the world. _The HistoryMakers Collection_ represents the _only_ massive attempt to record the black experience since the WPA Slave Narratives of the 1930s. The Library of Congress serves as our permanent repository.

[Ruby Dee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002039/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) was an American actress, poet, playwright, screenwriter, journalist and civil rights activist. She is best known for originating the role of "Ruth Younger" in the stage and film versions of [A Raisin in the Sun (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055353/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
She also starred in [The Jackie Robinson Story (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042609/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Cat People (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083722/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Do the Right Thing (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097216/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [American Gangster (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0765429/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Her film debut was [That Man of Mine (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0135671/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
For her performance as Mahalee Lucas in [American Gangster (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0765429/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), she was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress. As of 2019, she stands as the second oldest nominee for Best Supporting Actress, behind Gloria Stuart who was 87 when nominated for her role in Titanic for the 70th Academy Awards, 1998.  
  
Dee died on June 11, 2014, at her home in New Rochelle, New York, from natural causes at the age of 91.

# Trivia

## Ruby Dee

Edit

*   In 2008, at age 85, she became the second oldest actress to be nominated for an Academy Award. The oldest is [Gloria Stuart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001784/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Says her favorite quote comes from the book, "Charlotte's Web": "'Isn't life peculiar!' said Jeremy. 'Compared to what?' said the spider.".     
*   Attended and graduated from Hunter College with degrees in French and Spanish in 1944.     
*   Had appeared with her husband [Ossie Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001115/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) in nine films: [No Way Out (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042792/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Gone Are the Days! (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057112/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [The Sheriff (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067746/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Cool Red (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074352/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Roots: The Next Generations (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078678/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [All God's Children (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080350/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Do the Right Thing (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097216/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Jungle Fever (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102175/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) and [The Stand (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108941/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   2004: Recipient of the Kennedy Center Honors, along with [Elton John](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005056/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Joan Sutherland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0840116/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [John Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002354/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Warren Beatty](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000886/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) and husband [Ossie Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001115/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Had appeared with [Sidney Poitier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001627/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) in four films: [No Way Out (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042792/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Edge of the City (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050347/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [A Raisin in the Sun (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055353/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) and [Buck and the Preacher (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068323/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   1995: She and husband [Ossie Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001115/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) were awarded the American National Medal of the Arts from the National Endowment of the Arts in Washington, D.C.     
*   Ruby was an honorary member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc.     
*   In early 2003, she and her husband signed "Not In My Name", a statement opposing the impending invasion of Iraq. Other signatories included [Susan Sarandon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000215/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Noam Chomsky](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159008/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) and [Howard Zinn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0957016/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   1989: Voted into the NAACP image award Hall of Fame with husband [Ossie Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001115/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Lifelong friend of [Marla Gibbs](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004958/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Had three children: [Guy Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0204674/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Nora Day](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2091501/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), and [Hasna Muhammad](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm6744014/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Her ashes are inurned with Ossie at Ferncliff Cemetery and Mausoleum in Hartsdale, New York.     
*   She was a member of the NAACP, CORE, Student Non-Violent Coordinating Committee, Southern Christian Leadership Council.     
*   Ruby was one of 105 people invited to join AMPAS in 2008.     
*   Grandmother of [Muta'Ali](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1666093/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Has seven grandchildren.     
*   She appeared in two biopics of [Jackie Robinson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0732697/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) produced 40 years apart: [The Jackie Robinson Story (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042609/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) and [The Court-Martial of Jackie Robinson (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099311/?ref_=nmtrv_trv). She played his wife [Rachel Robinson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1201445/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) in the former and his mother Mallie in the latter.     
*   Had appeared with Sidney Poitier in four films: No Way Out (1950), Edge of the City (1957), A Raisin in the Sun (1961) and Buck and the Preacher (1972)." Also in "Go Man Go" (1954), as Poitier's wife.     
*   Aunt of [Tommy Wallace Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm6744013/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).

## **BIOGRAPHY**

[![Image 3: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/5062650_1.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/bio1.html)

Dominique Breckenridge

  
My name is Dominique Breckenridge, I am an art/film creative and fashion designer, of Dominique Revue and Dominique Private Collection.  
  
My trademark, professionally and personally, radiates from my adoration of classic cinema, influencing my continuous homage to Old Hollywood, rooted in my homebrew adage, "Classic entertainment in a modern world done in a vintage manner."  
  
As a self-taught artist and designer, creating and sewing clothes by hand as a hobby from an early age, which gained attention from my peers and others I encountered, encouraged me to design my first collection of garments, visibly built on my love for classic cinema.  
  
My artistic desire was inspired by my mom (a self-taught oil painter) and my dad (owner of his own construction company, realizing buildings from the ground up).  
  
From past to present, I have designed and created garments for the runway, as both a featured guest in fashion shows—choreographing and directing my segments personally—to writing, directing, choreographing, and creating all the garments in two of my own produced theatrical fashion shows—one inspired by Cab Calloway's **MINNIE THE MOOCHER** and another showcasing notable Black female entertainers in **BLACK WOMEN OF THE ARTS: 1920s—1950s**—to designing for individuals and myself—advertisement of my work in motion.  
  
My other creative work can best be described as a mood board displaying my expression as a visual person. From producing a mini-series, **[BETTYE: The Mini Series](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLLVf2x1YHSe-g_uzgttbQRIU68irv2O8m)**, based on my grand aunt Bettye Lightsy-Everett, who was the creator and owner of the first Black model studio in 1950s Chicago, to directing two documentaries, writing, directing, and producing a short film,**[BACKWARDS AND FORWARDS: For My Mom](https://backwardsandforwards.wixsite.com/shortfilm)**, creating classic cinema video edits in my personal time, and voicing my love for classic cinema on every platform I can, carving out an outlet to further display my passion for classic cinema, actors, and books in another house brew I call **[CINEMA COFFEE](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/)**—in frequent write-ups on films I recommend, book-to-screen adaptations, notable entertainers, repeat watches, coping through cinema, to films I could not live without— and chatting cinema and fashion on my YouTube Channel that also highlight my designs, discussing their influences by a particular film, actor, or their other inspiring contexts.  
  
And a project that is not only a near life-long passion of mine, but one that I am most proud of, I have recently completed writing a book adapted from an original script I wrote many years ago based on creating a world, unlike the historical stories we've left behind, and composing a fresh, original story, devising a period piece set in a parallel 1850s Victorian Era England-esque setting where all the leading characters looked like me, a person of color, living the life of titles, the season, and courting romances, in the landscape I created titled **[THE SOCIETY](https://thesocietyfilm.wixsite.com/reel/copy-of-reel-and-pitch-trailer)**.  
  
​You can see all of my work—and my homage to classic Hollywood—at **[dominiquerevue.weebly.com](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/)** or by viewing my**[Dominique Revue YouTube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/@DominiqueRevue)**and my **[Dominique Revue Productions YouTube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/@dominiquerevueproductions?app=desktop)**.

My write-ups, creative graphics, and video edits include Black actors, films, productions, comedians, musicians, and other entertainers in the world of classic cinema and the classic arts.

Credited as "the first leading Black actress to appear in a Broadway hit production" ... Hilda Simms

With a film career that only included three films, CHAMPION (1949), THE JOE LOUIS STORY (1953), BLACK WIDOW (1954), the actress began her career when she moved to NYC, joining the American Negro Theater, after assisting with a dramatic workshop at the Hampton Institute during WWII . . . **[Miss Hilda Simms](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)**[![Image 4: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/edna-mae-writeup-intro.jpg?1756143946)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)

Singer/actress Edna Mae Harris, dubbed "The Harlem Sweetheart"

Born in Harlem, singer/actress Edna Mae Harris, dubbed **["The Harlem Sweetheart"](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/enda-mae-harris.html)**performed in "soundies" and worked in major studio films—usually bit parts—BULLETS OR BALLOTS (1936), THE GREEN PASTURES (1936), THE GARDEN OF ALLAH (1936), to co-starring opposite Joe Louis in SPIRIT OF YOUTH (1938), and independent films by Oscar Micheaux

[![Image 5: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/francine-everett-writeup-intro-snap.jpg?1756143919)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/francine-everett.html)

"The Most Beautiful Woman in Harlem" ... Francine Everett.

With a career beginning as early as 16 as a chorus girl, before joining the Four Black Cats variety act, and becoming one of the first to enter Harlem's NEGRO PEOPLE'S THEATER—sponsored by the Works Progress Administration. . .**["The Most Beautiful Woman in Harlem,"](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/francine-everett.html)** Francine Everett, is yet another valuable entertainer of the Golden Age that should be recognized, remembered.[![Image 6: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/melba-liston-intro.jpg?1756143902)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/melba-liston.html)

 Jazz pioneer. . .Melba Liston

With the passing of Quincy Jones (November 3, 2024), aside from his incredible career, and initial shock on my part. . .Yes, I know, he was 91, but with people like Quincy Jones, you never see them leaving—for me, it was another performer that came to mind in the context of the many names that were mentioned as his fellow collaborators and connections. A name that may not have crossed your mind first. **[Jazz pioneer. . .Melba Liston](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/melba-liston.html)**.

[![Image 7: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/sallie-blair-intro-writeup.png?1756143875)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/sallie-blair.html)

"Season's hit singer," Miss Sallie Blair

Read my NEW writeup on the latest inductee to my NOTABLE ENTERTAINERS series, highlighting Black artists that are not as recognized as other talents on sight today . . . **["Season's hit singer," Miss Sallie Blair](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/sallie-blair.html)**[![Image 8: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/dark-manhattan-writeup-intro-snap.png?1756143882)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/dark-manhattan-1937.html)

A film beyond a recommendation. A film with context that should be seen, heard, and shared . . . DARK MANHATTAN (1937)

A film that was born to screen by Ralph Cooper, which made an impact on the Black film cycle in the late 1930s, **[DARK MANHATTAN (1937)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/dark-manhattan-1937.html)**

[![Image 9: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/whm-writeup-intro.jpg?1756143840)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/womens-history-month-classic-black-female-artists.html)

WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH 101: Classic Black Female Artists

For**[WOMENS HISTORY MONTH](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/womens-history-month-classic-black-female-artists.html)**, I wrote WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH 101: Classic Black Female Artists, to celebrate a few (of many) classic Black female artists—filmmakers, actors, writers, directors, entertainers, singers, pioneers in the history of cinema, stage, music, and literary works that should be household names to those who love the arts—a guide, including some recognizable names from my ongoing NOTABLE BLACK ENTERTAINERS series and some from my theatrical production BLACK WOMEN OF THE ARTS: 1920s—1950s that I hope creates a starting point into the history of Black female artists and their journey to express themselves through their works.[![Image 10: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/baker-by-murray-korman-taken-in-1936-cover-edit_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/notable-black-entertainers.html)

While hardly unknown, Josephine Baker was more than an entertainer.As showcased in my most recent pieces on La Baker​!  
  
Energetic, engaging, unfiltered, dynamic, any of these adjectives could describe La Baker. Romantic, optimistic, nurturing, poetic, philosopher, with a fantastic sense of humor and deep compassion for life, living, and the human condition, and as many facets to her life as there are descriptions to her personality. She has as much of a presence on paper in her own words as she does on screen, as vivid in writing as she is visually.  
  
Read my**_NEW_****[Voilà! La Baker: The Phenomenon That Was Josephine](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/voilagrave-la-baker-the-phenomenon-that-was-josephine.html)**write-up on[**FEARLESS AND FREE: A Memoir**by Josephine Baker](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/voilagrave-la-baker-the-phenomenon-that-was-josephine.html)and watch my new video**[](https://youtu.be/M1suiOsDf58?si=3CK_F4M1oQ3KIHNI)**about**[JOSEPHINE BAKER DAY](https://youtu.be/M1suiOsDf58?si=3CK_F4M1oQ3KIHNI)**

[![Image 11: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/katherine-dunham-cover-gif-graphic_orig.gif)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/notable-black-entertainers.html)

​It's 2025, and I still feel people are not fully digesting what a movement, what a moment Katherine Dunham was in her craft—dancing, choreographing, inventing—in every move she made.Dunham was a force. A force that should be as known as her contemporaries, in the conversation of artistry, and the commitment to your craft and creativity. Katherine Dunham's work was so rich, and her passion _makes_ you want to go out and create something. She was a champion of creativity; in whatever form it took, you had to create! The point was just to create something.  
  
My _**NEW**_ brief write-up about the impact of Dunham paired with my**[KATHERINE DUNHAM: She Is the Moment](https://youtu.be/xb2Gflrjlug)**video in my latest**[CINEMA COFFEE](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/katherine-dunham-she-is-the-moment.html)**piece.[![Image 12: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/amos-n-andy-banner-gif_orig.gif)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/notable-black-entertainers.html)

Regardless of where you stand on the controversy of the radio program or the television show, it is history. A history that should be discussed, particularly the roles these Black actors portrayed on the television screen.  
  
And while we cannot ignore its racial origins, to remove**AMOS 'N' ANDY**'s place in history is to erase these Black actors' work. And that . . . I cannot do. It's with these actors who brought life to these characters on the television screen that we will spend our time, to highlight a show that would air on television from 1951—1953,**THE AMOS 'N' ANDY SHOW**.  
  
Read my in-depth write-up,**[GIVING B(L)ACK OUR VOICE: A Moment with THE AMOS 'N' ANDY SHOW](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/giving-black-our-voice-a-moment-with-amos-andy----and-the-kingfish.html%E2%80%8B)**

"The first leading Black actress to appear in a Broadway hit production"

## HILDA SIMMS

July 20, 2024 |Updated January 23, 2026

Credited as "the first leading Black actress to appear in a Broadway hit production" . . . Hilda Simms.  
​

[![Image 2: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-painted_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Actress Hilda Simms has her portrait painted by Frank Slater, the date on the photo is June 28th, 1948. | During the portrait painting, Simms was starring in the stage production of ANNA LUCASTA, and the entire cast had their portraits painted.

​  
With a film career that only included two films—Simms is often credited in searches as the maid (who is employed by Marilyn Maxwell's character, Grace, who answers the phone and later opens the door when Kirk Douglas enters the flat), in**CHAMPION** (1949), however, the woman who acts in the film as the maid, _is not Hilda Simms_--**THE JOE LOUIS STORY** (1953), **BLACK WIDOW** (1954), the actress began her career when she moved to NYC, joining the American Negro Theater, after assisting with a dramatic workshop at the Hampton Institute during WWII—where she was awarded a teaching fellowship, teaching English and drama while pursuing her degree.  
  

[![Image 3: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/champion-1949.png?1768618449)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

The "maid" in CHAMPION (1949)

[![Image 4: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/champion-49.png?1768618461)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

The "maid" in CHAMPION (1949)[![Image 5: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/hilda-simms-right-meeting-soprono-leontyne-price.jpg?1768967695)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms (right) with soprano Leontyne Price | NYPL

[![Image 6: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-still_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms

  
After appearing in the play**THREE'S A FAMILY**, Simms's breakout role was in the stage production with the American Negro Theater in an all-Black cast of**ANNA LUCASTA**, where she played the title character, Anna Lucasta, in 1943, which successfully transitioned to Broadway in 1944.  
  
There is no denying Hilda Simms was a beauty. Some photos of Miss Simms radiate a Hedy Lamarr-esque likeness when photographed. There is also no denying that Hilda Simms had a grand acting talent and range that went unused as roles were unavailable to her and many Black actors of the time. A matter that frustrated Simms to a point she sought to provide an outlet for the very obstacles she faced.  
​​

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l0P3RVICQdA)[![Image 7: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-print-publication-for-the-onstage-production-of-anna-lucasta_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

  
More on that subject as we highlight the career of Hilda Simms.  
  

## anna lucasta

Starring Hilda Simms as the title character

[![Image 8: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-onstage-in-production-of-al_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Color (not colorized) print of Hilda Simms in/as ANNA LUCASTA, staged by American Negro Theater Company at NYC's Mansfield Theater | Photographed by: George Karger, 1945

[![Image 9: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-in-anna-lucasta-with-cast_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms (center) in the title role, staged by the American Negro Theatre Company at the Mansfield Theatre in NYC, (August 30, 1944 — November 30, 1946). | Photographed by: George Karge[![Image 10: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-in-anna-lucasta-with-other-cast_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms, John Tate as 'Danny', Kenneth Freeman as 'Lester' at His Majesty's Theatre in London, ENG | Photographed by: Kurt Hutton, 1947

[![Image 11: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-and-cast-of-anna-lucasta_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms (along with Canada Lee (L), Alice Childress and Alvin Childress) from the Broadway production of the American Negro Theatre's adaptation of Philip Yordan's play ANNA LUCASTA, adapted to screen in 1949 for Columbia starring Paulette Goddard in the title role, before returning to an all-Black cast in 1958 starring Eartha Kitt.

  
Showcased in the October 9, 1944 issue of LIFE magazine, Hilda Simms would later host her own radio program "Ladies Day" on NY WOV in 1954, and grace the cover page of JET magazine alongside co-star Sidney Poitier in 1955, for a piece showcasing "Two Examples of TV's New Policy Toward Negroes;" in how "A change in TV policy landed them starring roles."  
  
Simms co-starred with Poitier in 1955 on The Philco Television Playhouse program in the television play**A MAN IS TEN FEET TALL**, written by Robert Alan Aurthur, as husband-and-wife Tommy and Lucy Tyler.  
  
The character names may stand out to classic film fans, as the episode would later become a feature film directed by Martin Ritt in his directorial debut, **EDGE OF THE CITY**, in 1957, starring Poitier, reviving his role, alongside Ruby Dee as his onscreen wife Lucy Tyler, opposite John Cassavetes as Axel Nordman (portrayed by Don Murray in the television play).  
  

[![Image 12: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-pictured-with-earl-hollman-and-other-actors-from-the-harlem-theater_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms with fellow actor and co-star Earl Hollman (at her right) along with other fellow actors from the Harlem Theater[![Image 13: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-new-york-city-1944-canada-lee-langston-hughes-photographed-by-george-karger_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms, in New York City, 1944, along with fellow actor Canada Lee (center, Hilda Simms at his left), and Langston Hughes (front, right) | Photographed by George Karger

  
In the 1954 film **BLACK WIDOW**, Simms has a one-scene role that impacts the entire storyline. Providing a pivotal turning point for the lead male actor in the film, Van Heflin's "Peter Denver".Simms appears an hour and four minutes into the film and is on screen for three minutes. It takes only a fraction of those three minutes to see the natural and magnetic presence Simms projects on screen as an actress. Her character creates a memorable moment that stays with you for the rest of the film. At least for me. No matter how many times I've seen**BLACK WIDOW**, it's Hilda Simms I wait to see.  
  
This could be said of her lengthier role in**THE JOE LOUIS STORY**, and is true of her brief performance as Sidney Poitier's wife in**A MAN TEN FEET TALL**; however, with each of those performances, she is not given much to do, despite which, she manages to ignite a spark that you instinctively know can sizzle if given a character in which to work with. It prompts me to conceptualize what a career could have been paved ahead of her, had history been different, had racial inequality never existed throughout time.  
​  
  
  
  

[![Image 14: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/narrators-frederick-o-neal-and-hilda-simms.webp?1768620945)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Frederick O’Neal and Hilda Simms, as narrators to the 1959 educational audio program, GREAT NEGRO AMERICANS, distributed through the 1960—1970s, telling the stories of the achievements of Black Americans | Photo credit: Amistad Research Center

  
​Noticing this,I myself can only _imagine_ how she must have shined onstage during her run as Anna Lucasta, later portrayed by Eartha Kitt in the film adaptation in 1958, opposite Rex Ingram, Sammy Davis, Jr., Henry Scott, James Edwards, Frederick O'Neal, Rosetta LeNoire, and another unsung Black actress with a career that was cut short,**[Isabel Cooley](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/womens-history-month-classic-black-female-artists.html)**.  
  
Simms' range was such that she acted in the role of "Blanche DuBois" in an off-Broadway production of the Tennessee Williams play A STREETCAR NAMED DESIRE at the Peninsula Playhouse in Fish Creek, Wisconsin, with an all-White cast. Hilda would recall in 1959,_"It was great summer stock experience, but Fish Creek is so far off Broadway that I doubt very much if any producer saw us."_  
​  
At times, even Hilda Simms not looking "Black enough" caused her to lose parts, she herself saying this was something she heard often, saying so when considered for the part of a secretary in a Broadway play, ONLY IN AMERICA, stating her doubts in gaining the role,_"Producer Herman Shumlin likes me as an actress, but I don't look typically Negro enough. I've heard this line for the 1,000th time . . ."_ Not "Negro enough"?? To play a secretary?! How "Negro" are we supposed to look?! These comments, no matter when they are said, then or now, irritate me to near speechlessness. We come in all shades, a range of hair textures, and a variation of features, none the same.  
  

## LIFE Magazine

October 9, 1944

[![Image 15: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/editor/anna-lucasta.jpg?1768596054)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms in the October 9, 1944, 4-page spread issue of LIFE magazine[![Image 16: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/anna-lucasta-page-2.jpg?1768596040)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

[![Image 17: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/editor/anna-lucasta-page-3.jpg?1768595978)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)[![Image 18: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/anna-lucasta-page-4.jpg?1768596007)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

​  
As was the case with most Black actors of the era—restricted roles outside stereotypes in major studio films and productions—films like CARMEN JONES (1954), which should have sparked a wave of Black cinema in mainstream movies, proved to be the opposite . . .  
  

* * *

> We Negroes finally convinced the entertainment world not to stereotype us as just maids, porters and so on. But now too many producers are afraid to call us at all. Rather than do wrong, they do nothing.

—Dorothy Dandridge> Carmen Jones was the best break I've ever had. But no producer ever knocked on my door. There just aren't that many parts for a black actress.

—Dorothy Dandridge

* * *

[![Image 19: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/ebony-magazine-december-1945.jpg?1768620022)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

. . . causing actors like Simms unable to land steady—any—leading roles, in contrast to their contemporary white actors, many Black actors either maintain or turn to stage work, perform overseas, leave film and television work to seek other roles in the entertainment circuit, or retire from the business altogether.  
  
​Simms continued her stage work in the UK:**THE GENTLE PEOPLE**, in 1950,**HASSAN**at the Cambridge Theatre in London, England, in 1951, and in the US, even singing in Paris nightclubs under the name "Julie Riccardo."  
  
But in the 1950s,Hilda Simms' career would come under attack as Simms became blacklisted during the Red Scare, later writing an article for the PITTSBURGH COURIER, (read)**[“I’m No Benedict Arnold”](https://www.newspapers.com/image/40046754/?clipping_id=20575139&fcfToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJmcmVlLXZpZXctaWQiOjQwMDQ2NzU0LCJpYXQiOjE3MjE1ODM0ODcsImV4cCI6MTcyMTY2OTg4N30.HFs5wSkOaxm6mZ_viBpOIV_thKdDRw4xIJF6OIINaFo)**speaking candidly about the impediments of her career.  
  
In 1959, Hilda starred in her own one-woman stage show, AN EVENING WITH HILDA SIMMS, at the New School for Social Research in New York, booking the 500-seat auditorium that autumn in October and November, tailored to dramatic students.  
​​

* * *

[![Image 20: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/hilda-simms-jet-1959.jpg?1768622422)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

—excerpt via JET 1959

  
Hilda had a vision to create a place where aspiring actors could be taught and seen.  
​

[![Image 21: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/editor/img-20260119-212517.jpg?1768967200)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms inside the Park Motor Sales Showroom, for her role as the official hostess at the exposition, dated March 22, 1956, in New York City, New York

  
​Later, in the 1960s, Simms would return to television in a recurring role as Nurse Ayres in**THE DOCTORS AND THE NURSES**(1962—1964).  
​

[![Image 22: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/hilda-simms-radio-host.png?1768618988)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)[![Image 23: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-during-hassan_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

# Biography

## Ruby Dee

## [Overview](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002039/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_ql_1#overview)

*   Born[October 27](https://www.imdb.com/search/name/?birth_monthday=10-27&refine=birth_monthday&ref_=nmbio_bth_md), [1922](https://www.imdb.com/search/name/?birth_year=1922&ref_=nmbio_bth_yr) · [Cleveland, Ohio, USA](https://www.imdb.com/search/name/?birth_place=Cleveland%40%40%40%20Ohio%40%40%40%20USA&ref_=nmbio_bth_loc)   
*   Died[June 11](https://www.imdb.com/search/name/?death_date=2014-6-11&refine=death_monthday&ref_=nmbio_dth_md), [2014](https://www.imdb.com/search/name/?death_date=2014&ref_=nmbio_dth_yr) · [New Rochelle, New York, USA](https://www.imdb.com/search/name/?death_place=New%20Rochelle%40%40%40%20New%20York%40%40%40%20USA&ref_=nmbio_dth_loc) (natural causes)   
*   Birth name Ruby Ann Wallace   
*   Height 5′ 2¼″ (1.58 m)   

## [Mini bio](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002039/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_ql_1#mini_bio)

*   [Ruby Dee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002039/?ref_=nmbio_mbio) was an American actress, poet, playwright, screenwriter, journalist and civil rights activist. She is best known for originating the role of "Ruth Younger" in the stage and film versions of [A Raisin in the Sun (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055353/?ref_=nmbio_mbio).  
  
She also starred in [The Jackie Robinson Story (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042609/?ref_=nmbio_mbio), [Cat People (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083722/?ref_=nmbio_mbio), [Do the Right Thing (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097216/?ref_=nmbio_mbio), and [American Gangster (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0765429/?ref_=nmbio_mbio).  
  
Her film debut was [That Man of Mine (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0135671/?ref_=nmbio_mbio).  
  
For her performance as Mahalee Lucas in [American Gangster (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0765429/?ref_=nmbio_mbio), she was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress. As of 2019, she stands as the second oldest nominee for Best Supporting Actress, behind Gloria Stuart who was 87 when nominated for her role in Titanic for the 70th Academy Awards, 1998.  
  
Dee died on June 11, 2014, at her home in New Rochelle, New York, from natural causes at the age of 91.  
- IMDb mini biography by: Pedro Borges

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002039/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_ql_1#trivia)

*   In 2008, at age 85, she became the second oldest actress to be nominated for an Academy Award. The oldest is [Gloria Stuart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001784/?ref_=nmbio_trv).   
*   Says her favorite quote comes from the book, "Charlotte's Web": "'Isn't life peculiar!' said Jeremy. 'Compared to what?' said the spider.".   
*   Attended and graduated from Hunter College with degrees in French and Spanish in 1944.   
*   Had appeared with her husband [Ossie Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001115/?ref_=nmbio_trv) in nine films: [No Way Out (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042792/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [Gone Are the Days! (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057112/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [The Sheriff (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067746/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [Cool Red (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074352/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [Roots: The Next Generations (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078678/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [All God's Children (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080350/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [Do the Right Thing (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097216/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [Jungle Fever (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102175/?ref_=nmbio_trv) and [The Stand (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108941/?ref_=nmbio_trv).   
*   2004: Recipient of the Kennedy Center Honors, along with [Elton John](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005056/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [Joan Sutherland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0840116/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [John Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002354/?ref_=nmbio_trv), [Warren Beatty](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000886/?ref_=nmbio_trv) and husband [Ossie Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001115/?ref_=nmbio_trv).

## HILDA SIMMS

July 20, 2024 |Updated January 23, 2026

Credited as "the first leading Black actress to appear in a Broadway hit production" . . . Hilda Simms.  
​

[![Image 2: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-painted_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Actress Hilda Simms has her portrait painted by Frank Slater, the date on the photo is June 28th, 1948. | During the portrait painting, Simms was starring in the stage production of ANNA LUCASTA, and the entire cast had their portraits painted.

​  
With a film career that only included two films—Simms is often credited in searches as the maid (who is employed by Marilyn Maxwell's character, Grace, who answers the phone and later opens the door when Kirk Douglas enters the flat), in**CHAMPION** (1949), however, the woman who acts in the film as the maid, _is not Hilda Simms_--**THE JOE LOUIS STORY** (1953), **BLACK WIDOW** (1954), the actress began her career when she moved to NYC, joining the American Negro Theater, after assisting with a dramatic workshop at the Hampton Institute during WWII—where she was awarded a teaching fellowship, teaching English and drama while pursuing her degree.  
  

[![Image 3: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/champion-1949.png?1768618449)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

The "maid" in CHAMPION (1949)

[![Image 4: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/champion-49.png?1768618461)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

The "maid" in CHAMPION (1949)[![Image 5: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/hilda-simms-right-meeting-soprono-leontyne-price.jpg?1768967695)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms (right) with soprano Leontyne Price | NYPL

[![Image 6: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-still_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms

  
After appearing in the play**THREE'S A FAMILY**, Simms's breakout role was in the stage production with the American Negro Theater in an all-Black cast of**ANNA LUCASTA**, where she played the title character, Anna Lucasta, in 1943, which successfully transitioned to Broadway in 1944.  
  
There is no denying Hilda Simms was a beauty. Some photos of Miss Simms radiate a Hedy Lamarr-esque likeness when photographed. There is also no denying that Hilda Simms had a grand acting talent and range that went unused as roles were unavailable to her and many Black actors of the time. A matter that frustrated Simms to a point she sought to provide an outlet for the very obstacles she faced.  
​​

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l0P3RVICQdA)[![Image 7: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-print-publication-for-the-onstage-production-of-anna-lucasta_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

  
More on that subject as we highlight the career of Hilda Simms.  
  

## anna lucasta

[![Image 11: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-and-cast-of-anna-lucasta_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms (along with Canada Lee (L), Alice Childress and Alvin Childress) from the Broadway production of the American Negro Theatre's adaptation of Philip Yordan's play ANNA LUCASTA, adapted to screen in 1949 for Columbia starring Paulette Goddard in the title role, before returning to an all-Black cast in 1958 starring Eartha Kitt.

  
Showcased in the October 9, 1944 issue of LIFE magazine, Hilda Simms would later host her own radio program "Ladies Day" on NY WOV in 1954, and grace the cover page of JET magazine alongside co-star Sidney Poitier in 1955, for a piece showcasing "Two Examples of TV's New Policy Toward Negroes;" in how "A change in TV policy landed them starring roles."  
  
Simms co-starred with Poitier in 1955 on The Philco Television Playhouse program in the television play**A MAN IS TEN FEET TALL**, written by Robert Alan Aurthur, as husband-and-wife Tommy and Lucy Tyler.  
  
The character names may stand out to classic film fans, as the episode would later become a feature film directed by Martin Ritt in his directorial debut, **EDGE OF THE CITY**, in 1957, starring Poitier, reviving his role, alongside Ruby Dee as his onscreen wife Lucy Tyler, opposite John Cassavetes as Axel Nordman (portrayed by Don Murray in the television play).  
  

[![Image 12: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-pictured-with-earl-hollman-and-other-actors-from-the-harlem-theater_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms with fellow actor and co-star Earl Hollman (at her right) along with other fellow actors from the Harlem Theater[![Image 13: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-new-york-city-1944-canada-lee-langston-hughes-photographed-by-george-karger_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms, in New York City, 1944, along with fellow actor Canada Lee (center, Hilda Simms at his left), and Langston Hughes (front, right) | Photographed by George Karger

  
In the 1954 film **BLACK WIDOW**, Simms has a one-scene role that impacts the entire storyline. Providing a pivotal turning point for the lead male actor in the film, Van Heflin's "Peter Denver".Simms appears an hour and four minutes into the film and is on screen for three minutes. It takes only a fraction of those three minutes to see the natural and magnetic presence Simms projects on screen as an actress. Her character creates a memorable moment that stays with you for the rest of the film. At least for me. No matter how many times I've seen**BLACK WIDOW**, it's Hilda Simms I wait to see.  
  
This could be said of her lengthier role in**THE JOE LOUIS STORY**, and is true of her brief performance as Sidney Poitier's wife in**A MAN TEN FEET TALL**; however, with each of those performances, she is not given much to do, despite which, she manages to ignite a spark that you instinctively know can sizzle if given a character in which to work with. It prompts me to conceptualize what a career could have been paved ahead of her, had history been different, had racial inequality never existed throughout time.  
​  
  
  
  

[![Image 14: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/narrators-frederick-o-neal-and-hilda-simms.webp?1768620945)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Frederick O’Neal and Hilda Simms, as narrators to the 1959 educational audio program, GREAT NEGRO AMERICANS, distributed through the 1960—1970s, telling the stories of the achievements of Black Americans | Photo credit: Amistad Research Center

  
​Noticing this,I myself can only _imagine_ how she must have shined onstage during her run as Anna Lucasta, later portrayed by Eartha Kitt in the film adaptation in 1958, opposite Rex Ingram, Sammy Davis, Jr., Henry Scott, James Edwards, Frederick O'Neal, Rosetta LeNoire, and another unsung Black actress with a career that was cut short,**[Isabel Cooley](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/womens-history-month-classic-black-female-artists.html)**.  
  
Simms' range was such that she acted in the role of "Blanche DuBois" in an off-Broadway production of the Tennessee Williams play A STREETCAR NAMED DESIRE at the Peninsula Playhouse in Fish Creek, Wisconsin, with an all-White cast. Hilda would recall in 1959,_"It was great summer stock experience, but Fish Creek is so far off Broadway that I doubt very much if any producer saw us."_  
​  
At times, even Hilda Simms not looking "Black enough" caused her to lose parts, she herself saying this was something she heard often, saying so when considered for the part of a secretary in a Broadway play, ONLY IN AMERICA, stating her doubts in gaining the role,_"Producer Herman Shumlin likes me as an actress, but I don't look typically Negro enough. I've heard this line for the 1,000th time . . ."_ Not "Negro enough"?? To play a secretary?! How "Negro" are we supposed to look?! These comments, no matter when they are said, then or now, irritate me to near speechlessness. We come in all shades, a range of hair textures, and a variation of features, none the same.

October 9, 1944

Hilda Simms in the October 9, 1944, 4-page spread issue of LIFE magazine[![Image 16: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/anna-lucasta-page-2.jpg?1768596040)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

​  
As was the case with most Black actors of the era—restricted roles outside stereotypes in major studio films and productions—films like CARMEN JONES (1954), which should have sparked a wave of Black cinema in mainstream movies, proved to be the opposite . . .  
  

* * *

> We Negroes finally convinced the entertainment world not to stereotype us as just maids, porters and so on. But now too many producers are afraid to call us at all. Rather than do wrong, they do nothing.

—Dorothy Dandridge> Carmen Jones was the best break I've ever had. But no producer ever knocked on my door. There just aren't that many parts for a black actress.

—Dorothy Dandridge

* * *

[![Image 19: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/ebony-magazine-december-1945.jpg?1768620022)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

. . . causing actors like Simms unable to land steady—any—leading roles, in contrast to their contemporary white actors, many Black actors either maintain or turn to stage work, perform overseas, leave film and television work to seek other roles in the entertainment circuit, or retire from the business altogether.  
  
​Simms continued her stage work in the UK:**THE GENTLE PEOPLE**, in 1950,**HASSAN**at the Cambridge Theatre in London, England, in 1951, and in the US, even singing in Paris nightclubs under the name "Julie Riccardo."  
  
But in the 1950s,Hilda Simms' career would come under attack as Simms became blacklisted during the Red Scare, later writing an article for the PITTSBURGH COURIER, (read)**[“I’m No Benedict Arnold”](https://www.newspapers.com/image/40046754/?clipping_id=20575139&fcfToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJmcmVlLXZpZXctaWQiOjQwMDQ2NzU0LCJpYXQiOjE3MjE1ODM0ODcsImV4cCI6MTcyMTY2OTg4N30.HFs5wSkOaxm6mZ_viBpOIV_thKdDRw4xIJF6OIINaFo)**speaking candidly about the impediments of her career.  
  
In 1959, Hilda starred in her own one-woman stage show, AN EVENING WITH HILDA SIMMS, at the New School for Social Research in New York, booking the 500-seat auditorium that autumn in October and November, tailored to dramatic students.  
​​

* * *

[![Image 20: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/hilda-simms-jet-1959.jpg?1768622422)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

—excerpt via JET 1959

  
Hilda had a vision to create a place where aspiring actors could be taught and seen.  
​

[![Image 21: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/editor/img-20260119-212517.jpg?1768967200)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms inside the Park Motor Sales Showroom, for her role as the official hostess at the exposition, dated March 22, 1956, in New York City, New York

  
​Later, in the 1960s, Simms would return to television in a recurring role as Nurse Ayres in**THE DOCTORS AND THE NURSES**(1962—1964).  
​

[![Image 22: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/published/hilda-simms-radio-host.png?1768618988)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)[![Image 23: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-during-hassan_orig.png)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms during rehearsals for HASSAN (by James Elroy Flecker) at the Saville Theater in London, April 9th, 1951 ... | "The production is part of the Festival Season for the Festival of Britain, and Simms will star opposite André Huguenet." | Photographed by: Edward Miller

  
Credited with many accomplishments and accolades; "awarded a scholarship to St. Margaret's Academy," becoming "the first person of color to graduate from the institution," a member of the drama group at the University of Minnesota where she took courses, "studied Shakespeare with Harry Wagstaff Gribble; dramaturgy and voice with Dorothy Mower at the Goodman Theatre in Chicago; and speech and movement with Betty Cashman at Carnegie Hall in New York City, among other arts and language lessons."  
  
Despite her many achievements, Hilda Simms was still limited to the acting roles that were available for her and other Black women, leading her to become the Creative Arts Director for the New York State Human Rights Commission in the 1960s, frustrated by her own personal experiences and struggles with lack of Black roles for actors, to address this very problem within the entertainment industry.  
  

[![Image 24: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hildasimms_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)[![Image 25: Picture](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/uploads/3/2/1/0/3210008/hilda-simms-portrait-still_orig.jpg)](https://dominiquerevue.weebly.com/hilda-simms.html)

Hilda Simms | Photographed by Denis De Marney

 #### [1. Robin Givens](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002101/?ref_=ls_t_1) 

    *   Actress
    *   Director
    *   Producer

[Boomerang (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0103859/?ref_=ls_knf_1)

Robin Simone Givens was born on November 27, 1964 in New York City, to Ruth (Newby) and Reuben Givens. Her father left his family when Robin was a young girl, and she seldom saw him after that. Robin's mother raised her and her younger sister in Westchester, Connecticut. Her mother (once linked to Yankee outfielder [Dave Winfield](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0934889/?ls)) always encouraged her children's creativity, and helped them develop an interest in the arts. When she was young, Robin began playing the violin but quickly decided it was not for her. She chose instead to channel her artistic energy through acting and, at the age of ten, she started acting classes at the American Academy of Dramatic Arts in New York City. In 1980, at fifteen, Robin enrolled as a freshman at Sarah Lawrence College to study pre-med. By her junior year, however, Robin's excitement about the idea of a career in acting intensified and she began taking her craft more seriously. Robin's first experience in Hollywood was on [The Cosby Show (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086687/?ls), the hottest show on television. As a result of the role, she and comedian [Bill Cosby](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001070/?ls) forged a great friendship which would prove instrumental in Robin's career. She also landed a guest appearance on [Diff'rent Strokes (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077003/?ls). Her career was just about to take off. Robin first made it big in Hollywood in 1986. She took a role in a television movie, [Beverly Hills Madam (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090719/?ls), as "April Baxter". But, it was later that year that Robin became a recognizable actress in Hollywood. She was given a role on the television series [Head of the Class (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090444/?ls) as "Darlene Merriman". The series was a comedy about a group of gifted high school students that were placed in an enrichment class. In 1988, Robin married boxing legend [Mike Tyson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005512/?ls). This union put her into the national spotlight, as Tyson was on the top of his career. He was one of the youngest boxers ever to receive the attention, acclaim and financial success that Tyson garnered. The marriage ended (on Valentine's Day), just a year later. Rumors hinted at abuse and infidelity. Robin gave marriage another chance in 1997, by marrying her tennis instructor Svetozar Marinkovic. The marriage proved a total failure, as the two were separated since the day they married, and Robin filed for divorce citing "irreconcilable differences". Aside from a successful model and acclaimed actress, Robin is a mother. In October 1999, she gave birth to a baby boy. The baby's father is tennis player [Murphy Jensen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1654935/?ls), but the couple are no longer together. She has another child, and she is raising the two boys today. In 2000, Robin took a controversial career move as she took over for [Mother Love](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0366354/?ls) on the successful television talk show, [Forgive or Forget (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0194610/?ls). Her stint was brief, as just a few months later, the show stopped production. Many point to [Mother Love](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0366354/?ls)'s devoted audience, and the odd dismissal of her from the show she pioneered and created. Robin has tried to forge a friendship with [Mother Love](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0366354/?ls), but Love doesn't appear interested. Robin called in during a [Howard Stern](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001769/?ls) interview of [Mother Love](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0366354/?ls), where she said she was "on her way to work", which although innocent, proved to upset [Mother Love](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0366354/?ls).

 #### [2. Ruby Dee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002039/?ref_=ls_t_2)

[Ruby Dee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002039/?ls) was an American actress, poet, playwright, screenwriter, journalist and civil rights activist. She is best known for originating the role of "Ruth Younger" in the stage and film versions of [A Raisin in the Sun (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055353/?ls).  
  
She also starred in [The Jackie Robinson Story (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042609/?ls), [Cat People (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083722/?ls), [Do the Right Thing (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097216/?ls), and [American Gangster (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0765429/?ls).  
  
Her film debut was [That Man of Mine (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0135671/?ls).  
  
For her performance as Mahalee Lucas in [American Gangster (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0765429/?ls), she was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress. As of 2019, she stands as the second oldest nominee for Best Supporting Actress, behind Gloria Stuart who was 87 when nominated for her role in Titanic for the 70th Academy Awards, 1998.  
  
Dee died on June 11, 2014, at her home in New Rochelle, New York, from natural causes at the age of 91.

 #### [3. Regina Hall](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0356021/?ref_=ls_t_3)

    *   Producer

[One Battle After Another (2025)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt30144839/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

Regina Hall was born December 12, 1970 in Washington, D.C., to Ruby, a teacher, and Odie Hall, a contractor. She graduated from Fordham University in 1992, and went on to earn a master's degree in journalism from New York University before shifting to an acting career. In 1997 at age 26, she began appearing in commercials, and then made the giant leap into movies. Her fame came with her role in the comedy-horror spoof Scary Movie, Regina Hall has frequented the big screen in roles that far from betrayed her age. Her recurring role in Scary Movie and the sequel Scary Movie 2 exhibited the 30-year-old's ability to maintain her youthful appearance, as she portrayed the high-school-aged Brenda Meeks. However, her first film role was in the 1999 film The Best Man. The following year, she made many other film appearances, including her starring role in Scary Movie in 2000. She first had a role in the movie Love and Basketball which also starred close friend Sanaa Lathan. In 2001, Hall's list of credits grew to include her first television role, as Corretta Lipp on the prime-time drama Ally McBeal, which was a recurring role for several episodes. Furthermore, in 2001 Scary Movie 2 was released, in addition to the Mandel Holland comedy The Other Brother, featuring Hall as Vicki. One year later, she starred in the action-drama Paid in Full, directed by Charles Stone III. She would later on start in other films such as;Malibu's Most Wanted, Scary Movie 3, The Honeymooners, and First Sunday.

Audiences across the United States and internationally have admired her for her work- including her celebrated, Oscar-nominated performances in The Help (2011), Doubt (2008), and her Oscar winning performance in Fences (2016). Cicely Tyson was born in Harlem, New York City, where she was raised by her devoutly religious parents, who had come from the Caribbean island of Nevis. Her mother Theodosia was a domestic worker and her her father William was a carpenter and painter. Tyson was discovered by a fashion editor at Ebony Magazine, and with her stunning looks she quickly rose to the top of the modeling industry. In 1957 she began acting in Off-Broadway productions. She had small roles in feature films before she was cast as Portia in [The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063050/?ls). Four years later, she was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Actress for her sensational performance in the critically-acclaimed film [Sounder (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0069303/?ls). In 1974, she went on to portray a 110-year-old former slave in [The Autobiography of Miss Jane Pittman (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071175/?ls), which earned her two Emmy Awards. She also appeared in the television miniseries [Roots (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075572/?ls), [King (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077038/?ls), and [A Woman Called Moses (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078509/?ls). While Cicely has not appeared steadily onscreen because of her loyalty to solely portraying strong, positive images of Black women, she is definitely one of the most talented, beautiful actresses who ever graced stage or screen.

 #### [7. Grace Jones](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005063/?ref_=ls_t_7) 

    *   Music Artist
    *   Actress

[A View to a Kill (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090264/?ref_=ls_knf_7)

Grace Jones was in Spanish Town, St Catherine, Jamaica to [Marjorie Jones](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm9010296/?ls) (née Williams) and Reverend Robert W. Jones. When she was 12 she moved to Syracuse, New York, joining her family who had already moved there. She studied acting at Syracuse University and appeared in her first musical; halfway through college, she was approached by a drama professor who proposed that she work with him in a play he was putting on in Philadelphia, she accepted.  
  
Jones later moved to New York City and signed on as a model with Wilhelmina Models, but when her looks weren't successfully received, she moved to Paris, France, where her androgynous, bold, dark-skinned appearance was so highly visible, she began to model for [Yves Saint-Laurent](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0756721/?ls), [Claude Montana](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0598907/?ls), [Kenzo Takada](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0847025/?ls), [Helmut Newton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0628518/?ls), [Guy Bourdin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5120850/?ls), [Hans Feurer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1554626/?ls), and [Azzedine Alaïa](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0015823/?ls), and she appeared on the covers of "Elle", "Vogue", and "Der Stern."  
  
Disillusioned with modeling, and since she always wanted to be an actress, she began her movie career playing small parts, her first being in the blaxploitation flick [Gordon's War (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070124/?ls) followed by an uncomfortable cameo in the unwatchable French sex comedy [Let's Make a Dirty Movie (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072669/?ls). It wasn't until the the '80s that Jones' on-screen career really soared, when she appeared in three supporting roles: Zula, the amazonian warrior in the American sword and sorcery/adventure film [Conan the Destroyer (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087078/?ls); May Day, the secondary antagonist in the 14th James Bond film [A View to a Kill (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090264/?ls); and Katrina, a bloodthirsty Egyptian vampire queen in the comedy horror [Vamp (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0092147/?ls). Leaving audiences with only the resonance of unique and tantalizing movie performances, Jones hasn't acted in a feature film since the '90s.  
  
In recent years, Jones's primary focus is sharing the vulnerability behind her larger-than-life persona. Jones and director [Sophie Fiennes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0276400/?ls) released the documentary [Grace Jones: Bloodlight and Bami (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6903636/?ls). According to Fiennes, the documentary is not a retelling of what can easily be found in books and magazines, but an intimate portrait of Jones in recent years as she returns to Jamaica, the country of her birth and childhood, for a family reunion.
